::: {.store-lede}
One line per player per game with passing, rushing and receiving stats, fumbles, two-point conversions, touchdowns, field goals and extra points, and sacks and interceptions on defense. Regular season and playoffs are in the same file, told apart by season_type and game_type; the preseason is not included. A player has a row for each game in which he recorded at least one of these stats. Stats are added up from the play-by-play with nflfastR's rules; on a play with more than one lateral the yards can be credited differently from the official scoring. Tackles, passes defended, forced fumbles, punting and return yardage are not included.
:::

## Columns

One row per player per game. 46 columns. A row is identified by `game_id` + `player_id`.

```{=html}
<div class="store-dict"><table class="table">
<thead><tr>
<th>Column</th>
<th>Type</th>
<th>What it holds</th>
</tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>game_id</td><td>string</td><td>nflverse game id: season, week, away team and home team (2023_01_DET_KC); joins every NFL file.</td></tr>
<tr><td>season</td><td>int</td><td>NFL season, named for the year it starts (the 2023 season ends with the February 2024 Super Bowl).</td></tr>
<tr><td>season_type</td><td>string</td><td>REG for the regular season, POST for the playoffs.</td></tr>
<tr><td>game_type</td><td>string</td><td>Round of the season: REG (regular season), WC (wild card), DIV (divisional), CON (conference championship), SB (Super Bowl).</td></tr>
<tr><td>week</td><td>int</td><td>Week of the season; playoff weeks continue the count after the last regular-season week.</td></tr>
<tr><td>game_date</td><td>date</td><td>Date of the game in US Eastern time.</td></tr>
<tr><td>player_id</td><td>string</td><td>Player id: the NFL&#x27;s GSIS id (00-0033873), the same id used in the play-by-play file.</td></tr>
<tr><td>player_name</td><td>string</td><td>Player&#x27;s full name from the season roster; the gamebook abbreviation (P.Mahomes) where no roster entry matches.</td></tr>
<tr><td>position</td><td>string</td><td>Position group from the season roster: QB, RB (fullbacks included), WR, TE, OL, DL, LB, DB, K, P or LS.</td></tr>

<tr><td>passing_yards_after_catch</td><td>int</td><td>Passing yards gained by receivers after the catch.</td></tr>
<tr><td>passing_first_downs</td><td>int</td><td>First downs gained on completions.</td></tr>
<tr><td>passing_2pt_conversions</td><td>int</td><td>Two-point tries converted with a pass thrown by the player.</td></tr>
<tr><td>carries</td><td>int</td><td>Rushing attempts, scrambles and kneel-downs included.</td></tr>
<tr><td>rushing_yards</td><td>int</td><td>Rushing yards, including yards gained after taking a lateral on a run.</td></tr>
<tr><td>rushing_tds</td><td>int</td><td>Rushing touchdowns.</td></tr>
<tr><td>rushing_first_downs</td><td>int</td><td>First downs gained rushing.</td></tr>
<tr><td>rushing_2pt_conversions</td><td>int</td><td>Two-point tries converted by running the ball in.</td></tr>
<tr><td>targets</td><td>int</td><td>Passes thrown to the player, interceptions included.</td></tr>
<tr><td>receptions</td><td>int</td><td>Passes caught.</td></tr>

<tr><td>receiving_2pt_conversions</td><td>int</td><td>Two-point tries converted by catching the pass.</td></tr>
```

## Source and method

Source: nflverse (github.com/nflverse/nflverse-data), released under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 license, CC BY 4.0 (creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0): play-by-play from nflfastR, games and schedules as maintained by Lee Sharpe. Changes: columns were selected and renamed, a few repeated plays removed, and the game logs added up from the play-by-play.

The same file layout, IDs and column names are used for every season, so seasons stack without cleanup. See [how the store works](help.qmd) for formats, delivery and the license.

[Team Game Logs](nfl-team-logs.qmd) · [Play-by-Play](nfl-play-by-play.qmd) · [Games and Results](nfl-schedule.qmd) · [All NFL data](nfl.qmd)

::: {.faq-item}
### How do the NFL files join to each other?

On the ID columns. Game, team and player IDs are the same strings in every NFL file and every season, so a join on `game_id` (plus `team` or `player_id` where the grain needs it) lines them up.
:::

::: {.faq-item}
### Which games are included?

Every regular-season and playoff game, built from the open nflverse play-by-play. Regular season and postseason sit in the same file, told apart by `season_type`. Preseason and All-Star games are left out.
